title: Scalar adjunction and tensor realization in the coefficient ringed square
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Z}$ is exact for every scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. On ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] put $T_Z=L\operatorname{Ext}_{a_Z}$, $U_Z=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Z})$, $P_R=Lf_R^*$, $G_R=Rf_{R*}$, and similarly $P_S,G_S$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Take the small pro-etale sites small relative to the module-sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $E_{R,Z},E_{S,Z}$ for the fixed internal-module/section-module equivalences [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison, lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction], and use their specified derived operation and adjunction identifications. The section-ring coefficient maps define identity-underlying-topos morphisms $\phi_Z:(Z,S_Z)\to(Z,R_Z)$ and geometric ringed-topos morphisms $f_R,f_S$. Their coefficient square commutes with identity underlying commutation. Let $\theta:P_ST_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XP_R$ and $C:G_RU_X\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YG_S$ denote, after these identifications, the canonical ringed pullback and direct-image path comparisons of [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction], with ringed paths $f_R\circ\phi_X$ and $\phi_Y\circ f_S$ respectively.
The operation identifications carry $T_Z\dashv U_Z$ to $L\phi_Z^*\dashv R\phi_{Z*}$, including their unit and counit. Write $d^R,d^S$ for the actual derived geometric pullback tensor maps [def-sfb-module-object-projection-map] and $\mu_Z:T_Z(A\otimes_R^LB)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_ZA\otimes_S^LT_ZB$ for the scalar tensor comparison [def-sfb-internal-scalar-tensor-comparison]. They carry $\mu_Z$ to the canonical ringed derived tensor map $t_{\phi_Z}$, in this direction, with local generalized pure-tensor normalization $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ on flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Consequently, for all $A,B\in D(R_Y)$, the canonical ringed comparison $\theta$ satisfies
$$(\theta_A\otimes\theta_B)\circ d^S_{T_YA,T_YB}\circ P_S(\mu_{Y;A,B})
=\mu_{X;P_RA,P_RB}\circ T_X(d^R_{A,B})\circ\theta_{A\otimes_R^LB}.$$
This is an equality in the unbounded derived category of $S_X$-module objects, under the specified operation comparisons, without boundedness, constructibility or properness assumptions.

proof.text: Prove the ordinary coefficient square monoidal. The canonical internal scalar oplax structure is normalized on balanced pure tensors, so its adjoint restriction lax structure equals the canonical restriction structure. The restriction/direct-image comparison preserves generalized pure tensors, and the direct-image lax structures have the normalized same tensor pairing. Thus this comparison is monoidal. The scalar and geometric adjunctions are monoidal for these structures, so monoidal conjugation gives NatTrans.IsMonoidal for (pullIso a f).symm.hom.
Apply coefficientScalarSectionRealization separately at X and Y for the first two clauses.

Apply coefficientScalarDerivedTensorSquare to f and the ordinary monoidality just proved. Its conclusion is exactly the last clause. Combine these three clauses by conjunction introduction without changing the original statement or any geometric assumptions.
